statement: Every claim, number, and quote on the page comes from the Brief.
rationale: A landing page is a public statement; facts nobody approved can't appear on it.

statement: If a Container needs content the Brief lacks, leave the Container out and report it.
rationale: An empty or padded section reads worse than a shorter page.

statement: Report everything from the Brief that wasn't placed, with a one-line reason.
rationale: Reviewers need to see what the Build left out, not discover it.

statement: Skip internal notes, goals, and audience descriptions in the Brief; map only copy meant for the page.
rationale: Briefs mix instructions for the writer with copy for the reader.

statement: Use quotes verbatim from the Brief with the attribution it gives; never edit, merge, or invent them.
rationale: Quotes are approved word for word.

statement: Use the Brief's main headline as the hero heading; if it has none, base it on the key message.
rationale: The hero is the page's promise and should match what the Brief leads with.

statement: The hero eyebrow is the product or category name in two to four words, never a sentence.
rationale: The eyebrow orients the reader; the heading does the persuading.

examples.dont: The fastest way to understand your data

statement: Map each Brief section that has a heading and body copy to a Media With Section.
rationale: One idea per section keeps the page scannable.

statement: Use a Content Grid for two to six short, parallel items, with a Subheading as each title.
rationale: Parallel items read best side by side.

statement: Use a Callout for a boxed proof point or aside inside the section it supports.
rationale: Proof sits next to the claim it backs up.

statement: Turn the Brief's questions and answers into the FAQ, one question per item.
rationale: The FAQ answers objections the Brief already anticipates.

statement: Use one Speed Bump per page, last, for the closing call to action.
rationale: Readers who reach the end need one clear next step.

statement: Never place two Heading blocks in a row; follow a Heading with Text or supporting copy.
rationale: Two headings in a row break the document outline.

statement: Italic display text must be an exact whole-word suffix of its heading, and shorter than the rest.
rationale: The italic phrase is an accent, not half the heading.

statement: Label the primary CTA "Book a demo" and the secondary "Start for free".
rationale: Consistent labels make the conversion path predictable.

statement: Put CTAs in the hero and in the closing Speed Bump.
rationale: Readers convinced early and readers who finish both need a next step.

statement: Copy CTA URLs from the Brief verbatim, and never invent campaign or tracking parameters.
rationale: Tracking parameters belong to the campaign owner.

statement: Fill each media slot with an Image library entry that shows what the section describes, before considering generation.
rationale: Library images are approved and real.

statement: Never generate an image of the product's UI; use a library screenshot or leave a Placeholder.
rationale: A generated screenshot is a fabricated product claim.

statement: Generate an image only for an illustrative slot with no library match: abstract, no text, no logos.
rationale: Abstract illustrations add rhythm without implying anything about the product.

statement: Leave a media slot empty as a Placeholder only when no library image fits and generation isn't allowed; report it.
rationale: A person fills it before publishing.

statement: Use sentence case in titles, headings, and CTAs; capitalize only proper nouns.
rationale: Sentence case reads faster and stays consistent.

statement: Don't end titles or headings with a period.
rationale: Headings are labels, not sentences.

statement: Use active voice.
rationale: Active voice says who does what.

statement: Use the Oxford comma.
rationale: It removes ambiguity in lists.

statement: Never hyperlink the word "here"; link specific, descriptive words.
rationale: Descriptive links help scanning and accessibility.

statement: Write alt text that says what the image shows, not what the section claims.
rationale: Alt text is for people who can't see the image.

statement: Proofread every line: no spelling, grammar, or punctuation errors.
rationale: Errors undercut every claim on the page.

statement: Never name competitors; describe the category instead.
rationale: Comparisons belong on pages built for them, with legal review.

statement: Write plainly and specifically; prefer a concrete example to an adjective.
rationale: Specific copy is more credible than enthusiastic copy.

statement: When the Brief gives no meta title, base it on the hero heading.
rationale: The meta title should match what the page promises.

statement: Keep slugs to three to six words, lead with the topic, and leave out dates and filler.
rationale: Short, topical slugs read well and age well.
